steps.label: Trachea and central bronchi
steps.detail: Follow the trachea and main and lobar bronchi for narrowing, intraluminal material and extrinsic compression.
steps.look: Thin-section axial images with multiplanar and minimum-intensity projections along the airway.
steps.normal: Trachea and central bronchi patent with normal calibre and wall.
findings: Tracheal stenosis at [ ], __ mm long, minimum lumen __ mm (post-intubation pattern).
Endobronchial lesion in the [ ] bronchus.
Circumferential wall thickening sparing the posterior membrane (relapsing polychondritis / tracheobronchopathia pattern).
steps.tip: Diseases of the cartilage spare the posterior membrane; dependent mucus can mimic an endobronchial lesion.

steps.label: Bronchiectasis
steps.detail: Describe distribution and morphology, lack of tapering and bronchi visible near the pleura.
steps.look: Compare each bronchus with its accompanying artery (signet ring); follow bronchi to the periphery.
findings: [Cylindrical / varicose / cystic] bronchiectasis in the [ ] lobes.
Traction bronchiectasis within fibrosis.
steps.tip: Traction bronchiectasis belongs to the surrounding fibrosis and is interpreted with it.

steps.label: Small airways
steps.detail: Map centrilobular nodules, tree-in-bud change and mucus plugging.
steps.look: Lung windows in the periphery.
steps.normal: No tree-in-bud or centrilobular nodules; no mucus plugging.
findings: Tree-in-bud nodules in the [ ], compatible with infectious bronchiolitis.
Mucus plugging of the [ ] bronchi.

steps.label: Expiratory imaging
steps.detail: Assess air trapping and dynamic central airway collapse when expiratory images are acquired.
steps.look: Paired inspiratory and expiratory images at the same levels.
steps.normal: Expiratory images: no air trapping; no excessive central airway collapse.
findings: Lobular air trapping in the [ ].
Expiratory collapse of the trachea by more than __%.
Expiratory imaging not acquired; air trapping not assessed.
steps.tip: Mosaic attenuation can reflect air trapping, vascular disease or infiltrates; expiration separates them.

steps.label: Consequences
steps.detail: Look for collapse, post-obstructive infection and an obstructing mass.
steps.look: Lobes distal to a narrowed airway.
steps.normal: No atelectasis, consolidation or obstructing mass.
findings: [Right upper lobe] collapse distal to an obstructing lesion.
Post-obstructive consolidation.

steps.label: Projection and quality
steps.detail: Check projection, position, rotation, inspiration, exposure and coverage.
steps.look: Spinous processes midway between the clavicular heads; about 6 anterior ribs above the diaphragm; lung apices and costophrenic angles included.
steps.normal: PA erect radiograph, adequately inspired, not rotated, with adequate exposure.
findings: AP supine radiograph; heart size cannot be assessed reliably.
Rotated to the [right]; mediastinal contours are distorted.
Poor inspiration; basal opacity may be exaggerated.
steps.tip: Compare with prior imaging first: the change is often the finding.

steps.label: Airway, mediastinum, hila and heart
steps.detail: Inspect the trachea, mediastinal lines, hila, heart size and aortic contours.
steps.look: Trachea midline; right paratracheal stripe; aortopulmonary window; azygo-oesophageal line; both hila; cardiothoracic ratio on a PA film.
steps.normal: Trachea central; normal mediastinal contours and hila; heart size normal.
findings: Cardiomegaly (cardiothoracic ratio __ on a PA film).
Enlarged [right / bilateral] hilum.
Widened superior mediastinum.
Obliterated aortopulmonary window.
steps.tip: Look behind the heart and at the hila: they are hidden areas where masses and consolidation are missed.

steps.label: Lungs
steps.detail: Describe the pattern (consolidation, interstitial, nodules or masses, lucency), its distribution and any volume loss.
steps.look: Compare both lungs zone by zone; use the silhouette sign to localise opacities.
findings: Consolidation in the [right middle lobe] with loss of the [right heart border] (silhouette sign).
Upper-lobe venous diversion, Kerley B lines and peribronchial cuffing (interstitial oedema).
Solitary pulmonary nodule __ mm in the [ ].
Lobar collapse of the [left lower lobe] (sail sign behind the heart).
steps.tip: The silhouette sign localises an opacity: loss of the heart border means the lingula or middle lobe.

steps.label: Pleura and diaphragm
steps.detail: Check apices and costophrenic angles, supine pneumothorax signs and free gas under the diaphragm.
steps.look: Apices, lateral chest wall, costophrenic angles; deep sulcus sign on supine films; below the diaphragm.
steps.normal: No pleural effusion or pneumothorax; normal diaphragm; no free subdiaphragmatic gas.
findings: [Right] pleural effusion with a meniscus.
[Left] apical pneumothorax with a visible pleural line, __ cm at the apex.
Deep sulcus sign on a supine radiograph (anterior pneumothorax).
Free gas beneath the right hemidiaphragm.
steps.tip: On a supine film a pneumothorax collects anteriorly and basally.

steps.label: Devices, bones and review areas
steps.detail: Trace every tube and line to its tip and review bones, soft tissues and the upper abdomen.
steps.look: Endotracheal tube tip above the carina; central line tip at the cavoatrial junction; nasogastric tube below the diaphragm in the stomach.
steps.normal: No tubes or lines. Bones and soft tissues unremarkable.
findings: Endotracheal tube tip __ cm above the carina.
Central venous catheter tip in the [ ].
Nasogastric tube coiled in the oesophagus — reposition before use.
Rib fractures of the [ ] ribs.
steps.tip: A nasogastric tube must pass below the diaphragm and deviate to the left into the stomach.

steps.label: Parenchymal pattern
steps.detail: Describe ground glass, consolidation, crazy paving and associated vascular or septal changes.
steps.look: Thin-section lung windows.
findings: Multifocal ground-glass opacities with crazy paving.
Ground glass with vascular enlargement within the opacities.
Organising pattern: consolidation with subpleural bands and reversed halo.

steps.label: Distribution and extent
steps.detail: Map laterality, lobes and peripheral or central predominance; estimate extent.
steps.look: Coronal reformats; score each lobe for extent.
findings: Bilateral, peripheral and lower-lobe predominant.
CT involvement score __/25.
Unilateral central distribution.
steps.tip: Bilateral, peripheral, multifocal ground glass is the typical distribution.

steps.label: Features favouring another cause
steps.detail: Seek findings supporting another process.
steps.look: Tree-in-bud, cavitation, lobar consolidation, effusions, septal lines and cardiomegaly.
steps.normal: No features to suggest an alternative diagnosis.
findings: Tree-in-bud and centrilobular nodules (bronchopneumonia pattern).
Septal thickening with effusions and cardiomegaly (oedema pattern).
Lobar consolidation.

steps.label: Associated findings
steps.detail: Review pleura, nodes and complications such as pulmonary embolism when contrast was given.
steps.look: Pleural spaces, mediastinum and pulmonary arteries if opacified.
findings: Pulmonary embolism in the [ ] arteries.
Pneumomediastinum.
Mediastinal lymphadenopathy.

steps.label: Comparison and CO-RADS
steps.detail: State interval change and, when appropriate for the setting, the CO-RADS category with its supporting pattern.
steps.look: Prior imaging; the clinical context in which CO-RADS applies.
findings: CO-RADS 5: typical features.
CO-RADS 3: equivocal features.
CO-RADS 2: features typical of another infection.
Interval [improvement / progression] since [date].
steps.tip: CO-RADS expresses suspicion in its intended setting and does not confirm infection.

steps.label: Cyst morphology
steps.detail: Confirm true cysts and describe wall, shape and size range.
steps.look: Thin sections: a cyst has a thin perceptible wall; separate from emphysema (no wall, central dot) and bronchiectasis (connected to airways).
findings: Round thin-walled cysts __–__ mm, uniformly distributed (LAM pattern).
Bizarre-shaped cysts with nodules (Langerhans cell histiocytosis pattern).
Lentiform subpleural and paramediastinal cysts (Birt–Hogg–Dubé pattern).
steps.tip: A thin-walled lucency is not automatically a cyst; exclude emphysema and bronchiectasis first.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Assess zonal, axial and subpleural distribution and costophrenic involvement.
steps.look: Coronal reformats: upper versus lower, central versus peripheral.
findings: Upper-zone predominance with sparing of the costophrenic angles.
Diffuse distribution including the bases.
Lower-zone, subpleural and paramediastinal predominance.
steps.tip: Sparing of the costophrenic angles is characteristic of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

steps.label: Associated nodules
steps.detail: Look for nodules and cavitating nodules and their relation to cysts.
steps.look: Lung windows for centrilobular and cavitating nodules.
findings: Centrilobular and cavitating nodules in the upper zones.

steps.label: Background lung
steps.detail: Assess ground glass, septal thickening and fibrosis.
steps.look: Lung parenchyma between cysts.
findings: Ground glass with perivascular cysts (LIP pattern).
Ground glass with small cysts (DIP pattern).

steps.label: Context and complications
steps.detail: Review pneumothorax and relevant extrapulmonary findings.
steps.look: Pleura; upper abdomen for renal angiomyolipomas or tumours; chylous effusion.
steps.normal: No pneumothorax or relevant extrapulmonary finding.
findings: Pneumothorax on the [ ].
Renal angiomyolipomas in the upper abdomen (tuberous sclerosis / LAM).
Renal lesion in the upper abdomen (Birt–Hogg–Dubé context).

steps.label: Lumen and calibre
steps.detail: Review calibre, dilatation and luminal contents along the covered course.
steps.look: Contrast swallow or CT from the pharyngo-oesophageal junction to the gastro-oesophageal junction.
steps.normal: Normal oesophageal calibre without retained contents.
findings: Dilated oesophagus with retained fluid and debris and a smooth tapered gastro-oesophageal junction (achalasia pattern).
Hiatus hernia with [ ] cm of stomach above the diaphragm.

steps.label: Wall and mucosa
steps.detail: Describe mural or mucosal abnormalities.
steps.look: Double-contrast mucosal detail on fluoroscopy; wall thickness on CT.
findings: Irregular mucosal thickening over __ cm.
Plaques or ulcers compatible with oesophagitis.
Asymmetric wall thickening __ mm on CT.

steps.label: Rings, webs and strictures
steps.detail: Characterise rings, webs and strictures by site, length and contour.
steps.look: Distended views; smooth tapered versus irregular shouldered narrowing.
findings: Lower oesophageal (Schatzki) ring.
Smooth tapered stricture at the gastro-oesophageal junction __ cm long (peptic pattern).
Irregular shouldered stricture __ cm long, suspicious for carcinoma.
steps.tip: Irregular, shouldered narrowing is suspicious for tumour; smooth tapered narrowing is usually benign.

steps.label: External impressions
steps.detail: Distinguish intrinsic disease from vascular or other external impressions.
steps.look: Relation to the aortic arch, aberrant subclavian artery, left atrium and mediastinal masses.
findings: Posterior oblique impression from an aberrant right subclavian artery.
Extrinsic compression by a mediastinal mass.

steps.label: Acute complications
steps.detail: Assess leak, periesophageal gas, mediastinal inflammation and nodes.
steps.look: Water-soluble contrast for leak; CT for pneumomediastinum and effusion.
steps.normal: No leak, pneumomediastinum or mediastinal collection.
findings: Contrast leak from the left posterolateral distal oesophagus with pneumomediastinum and left effusion (Boerhaave pattern).
Mediastinal collection __ mm.
steps.tip: Boerhaave rupture typically involves the left posterolateral distal oesophagus.

steps.label: Dominant pattern
steps.detail: Identify the dominant pattern: reticular, nodular, high attenuation or low attenuation.
steps.look: Thin-section inspiratory images; relate findings to the secondary pulmonary lobule.
findings: Reticular pattern with honeycombing.
Nodular pattern with [perilymphatic / centrilobular / random] distribution.
Ground-glass opacity with [crazy paving / mosaic attenuation].
Low attenuation: [centrilobular emphysema / cysts].
steps.tip: Classify nodules by their relation to the lobule and pleura: perilymphatic, centrilobular or random.

steps.label: Distribution
steps.detail: Assess upper or lower, central or peripheral predominance and subpleural sparing.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal reformats.
findings: Basal and subpleural predominance.
Upper-zone and peribronchovascular predominance.
Subpleural sparing (NSIP pattern).

steps.label: Fibrosis
steps.detail: Assess architectural distortion, traction bronchiectasis, honeycombing and volume loss; classify the UIP pattern.
steps.look: Honeycombing as clustered subpleural cysts in layers; prone images to separate dependent opacity.
findings: UIP pattern: basal subpleural honeycombing with traction bronchiectasis.
Probable UIP: basal subpleural reticulation with traction bronchiectasis, no honeycombing.
Fibrosis with features of an alternative diagnosis: [ ].
steps.tip: Dependent opacity and poor inspiration can mimic interstitial disease; prone images resolve it.

steps.label: Airways and air trapping
steps.detail: Assess airways and expiratory air trapping when obtained.
steps.look: Expiratory images at matching levels.
steps.normal: No airway abnormality; no air trapping on expiration.
findings: Lobular air trapping on expiration with mosaic attenuation (hypersensitivity pneumonitis pattern with fibrosis).
Expiratory imaging not acquired.

steps.label: Comparison and context
steps.detail: Review progression and relevant pleural, oesophageal and nodal clues.
steps.look: Matching prior images; oesophagus, pleura and nodes.
findings: Progression of fibrosis since [date].
Dilated oesophagus (systemic sclerosis context).
Pleural plaques (asbestos exposure).

steps.label: Primary tumour
steps.detail: Record site, total size and, for a part-solid lesion, the solid component.
steps.look: Lung windows in the plane of maximal extent; measure the solid component separately in part-solid tumours.
findings: [Solid] tumour in the [right upper lobe], __ mm.
Part-solid lesion __ mm with a solid component of __ mm (T category by solid component).
steps.tip: In part-solid tumours the T category depends on the solid (invasive) component size.

steps.label: Local extent (T descriptors)
steps.detail: Check airway involvement, atelectasis, pleura, chest wall, mediastinum and separate nodules.
steps.look: Soft-tissue and lung windows; relation to the main bronchus, carina, pleura and mediastinal structures.
findings: Involvement of the main bronchus without carina involvement, with atelectasis to the hilum (T2).
Chest wall invasion (T3).
Invasion of the mediastinum / great vessels / carina (T4).
Separate nodule in the same lobe (T3) / different ipsilateral lobe (T4).

steps.label: Regional nodes
steps.detail: Name suspicious stations and laterality; separate single-station from multiple-station N2 disease.
steps.look: IASLC nodal map; short axis at each station.
steps.normal: No suspicious hilar or mediastinal nodes.
findings: Ipsilateral hilar node (N1).
Single ipsilateral mediastinal station [4R] (N2a).
Multiple ipsilateral mediastinal stations (N2b).
Contralateral mediastinal or supraclavicular node (N3).
steps.tip: Station 1 (supraclavicular) nodes are N3 on either side.

steps.label: Distant disease
steps.detail: Inspect pleura, pericardium, contralateral lung, adrenals, liver and imaged bones.
steps.look: Pleural surfaces; adrenals and liver on the upper abdominal coverage; bones.
steps.normal: No pleural, contralateral lung or extrathoracic metastases in the field.
findings: Pleural nodules / malignant effusion (M1a).
Single extrathoracic metastasis in the [adrenal] (M1b).
Multiple extrathoracic metastases in [one / several] organ systems (M1c1 / M1c2).

steps.label: Imaging stage
steps.detail: Summarise imaging T, N and M with the TNM edition and the findings whose confirmation would change stage.
steps.look: Combine the descriptors above; name the edition.
findings: Clinical imaging stage (TNM 9th edition): cT__ cN__ cM__.
Stage depends on confirmation of [ ] by [EBUS / PET-CT / biopsy].

steps.label: Compartment
steps.detail: Localise the lesion to the prevascular, visceral or paravertebral compartment.
steps.look: Axial and sagittal images; the epicentre defines the compartment.
findings: Prevascular (anterior) mediastinal mass __ × __ mm.
Visceral (middle) mediastinal mass.
Paravertebral (posterior) mass extending into the neural foramen.
steps.tip: Localise the epicentre first; each compartment has its own differential.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Assess soft tissue, fluid, fat, calcification and enhancement.
steps.look: CT attenuation before and after contrast.
findings: Fluid-attenuation cyst with a thin wall (e.g., bronchogenic or pericardial cyst).
Fat, fluid and calcification (teratoma pattern).
Homogeneous soft-tissue mass with enhancement.

steps.label: Local relationships
steps.detail: Assess displacement or invasion of vessels, airway and oesophagus.
steps.look: Fat planes around the mass; vessel and airway calibre.
steps.normal: No compression or invasion of adjacent structures.
findings: Compression of the superior vena cava.
Tracheal displacement / narrowing.
Invasion of the pericardium.

steps.label: Nodal stations
steps.detail: Identify involved nodal stations and morphology.
steps.look: IASLC map: stations 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10; short axis.
steps.normal: No enlarged mediastinal or hilar nodes.
findings: Enlarged nodes in stations [4R, 7], short axis up to __ mm.
Necrotic nodes.
Calcified nodes.
steps.tip: Assign stations by their anatomic landmarks, not by proximity to a large vessel.

steps.label: Other thoracic findings
steps.detail: Review lungs, pleura, spinal canal and chest wall extension.
steps.look: Lung windows; neural foramina for paravertebral masses.
findings: Extension into the spinal canal through the neural foramen.
Pleural deposits.

steps.label: Pathway
steps.detail: Choose the incidental, screening or known-malignancy pathway and check exclusions.
steps.look: Referral context: age, cancer history, immune status and screening programme.
findings: Incidental nodule in a patient aged __ without cancer or immunosuppression: Fleischner 2017 applies.
Screening context: the programme protocol applies, not Fleischner.
Known malignancy: follow the oncology context, not Fleischner.
steps.tip: Fleischner guidance does not apply to screening, patients under 35, immunocompromise or known cancer.

steps.label: Nodule type and location
steps.detail: Record location and whether each nodule is solid, pure ground glass or part-solid.
steps.look: Thin sections (1.5 mm or less); lung windows.
findings: Solid nodule in the [right upper lobe] (series __ image __).
Pure ground-glass nodule in the [ ].
Part-solid nodule in the [ ].

steps.label: Size and morphology
steps.detail: Measure mean diameter or volume and assess margins, fat, calcification and perifissural shape.
steps.look: Average of long and short axes in the plane of maximal dimension; bone window for calcification.
findings: Solid nodule, mean diameter __ mm, [smooth / lobulated / spiculated].
Benign calcification pattern ([diffuse / central / laminated / popcorn]).
Intranodular fat (hamartoma).
Perifissural nodule: smooth, triangular or lentiform, attached to the fissure.
steps.tip: A perifissural nodule needs the complete benign morphology, not only proximity to a fissure.

steps.label: Interval change
steps.detail: Compare with prior CT using comparable reconstructions.
steps.look: Same slice thickness and kernel; volumetry when available.
findings: Stable since [date] (__ years).
Growth from __ to __ mm since [date].
New solid component in a previously pure ground-glass nodule.

steps.label: Assessment and recommendation
steps.detail: Identify the most suspicious nodule and give a recommendation with the guideline and its rationale.
steps.look: Apply the chosen guideline to the most suspicious nodule.
findings: Solid nodule under 6 mm in a low-risk patient: no routine follow-up (Fleischner 2017).
Solid nodule 6–8 mm: CT at 6–12 months (Fleischner 2017).
Nodule over 8 mm: consider CT at 3 months, PET-CT or tissue sampling.

steps.label: Parenchyma
steps.detail: Describe consolidation, nodules and cavities.
steps.look: Upper-lobe apical and posterior segments and superior segments of the lower lobes; lung windows.
findings: Upper-lobe consolidation with cavitation __ mm (post-primary pattern).
Consolidation in the [ ] with ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (primary pattern).
steps.tip: Cavitation and tree-in-bud spread suggest active, potentially transmissible disease.

steps.label: Spread pattern
steps.detail: Distinguish endobronchial (tree-in-bud) from miliary spread.
steps.look: Thin-section CT: tree-in-bud versus uniformly distributed random micronodules.
findings: Tree-in-bud nodules in the [ ] (endobronchial spread).
Innumerable random 2–3 mm nodules (miliary pattern).

steps.label: Nodes
steps.detail: Review nodal stations and internal necrosis or calcification.
steps.look: Hilar and mediastinal nodes on contrast-enhanced CT.
findings: Necrotic (low-attenuation centre, rim-enhancing) mediastinal nodes.
Calcified hilar nodes (healed).

steps.label: Pleura and airways
steps.detail: Assess effusion, pleural thickening and airway narrowing.
steps.look: Pleural spaces; central bronchi.
steps.normal: No pleural effusion or thickening; airways normal.
findings: [Right] pleural effusion.
Empyema with split pleura sign.
Bronchial stenosis.

steps.label: Sequelae and comparison
steps.detail: Assess scarring, volume loss, calcified granulomas and interval activity.
steps.look: Prior imaging for change.
findings: Apical fibrosis with volume loss and calcified granulomas (inactive, healed disease).
New cavitation compared with [date] (reactivation).
steps.tip: Imaging suggests activity but cannot prove the organism or the stage of infection.

steps.label: Location and shape
steps.detail: Localise to the thymic region and assess contour and size with the patient's age.
steps.look: Prevascular mediastinum; normal thymus is triangular or bilobed with straight or concave margins.
findings: Diffusely enlarged thymus with preserved shape (hyperplasia pattern).
Round / lobulated focal mass __ × __ mm in the thymic region.
steps.tip: Normal and rebound thymus can look mass-like in young patients; age and shape are key.

steps.label: Composition
steps.detail: Identify fat, fluid, soft tissue and calcification.
steps.look: CT attenuation.
findings: Fluid-attenuation thymic cyst.
Soft-tissue mass with calcification.
Fat, fluid and calcification (teratoma).

steps.label: MRI characterisation
steps.detail: Describe chemical-shift signal loss and T1/T2 signal.
steps.look: In- and opposed-phase MRI.
findings: Signal loss on opposed-phase images: thymic hyperplasia.
No signal loss: soft-tissue lesion such as thymoma or lymphoma.
steps.tip: Chemical-shift signal drop indicates fat within the gland and favours hyperplasia over thymoma.

steps.label: Enhancement and invasion
steps.detail: Assess enhancement and relation to vessels and pericardium.
steps.look: Contrast-enhanced images; fat planes with the great vessels and pericardium.
findings: Invasion of the [pericardium / great vessels] (invasive thymoma or thymic carcinoma).

steps.label: Pleura and nodes
steps.detail: Review pleural deposits, nodes and interval change.
steps.look: Pleural surfaces for drop metastases; nodal stations.
findings: Pleural drop metastases.
Mediastinal lymphadenopathy (thymic carcinoma or lymphoma).
Interval change since [date].
